citeinfo.title: Applied Biosolids Data Input Summed from Fields to National Hydrography Dataset Plus V2 in Virginia, 2024

descript.abstract: This metadata record contains two tables with reported and calculated amounts of biosolids applied to agricultural land within Virginia in 2024 at different scales. Included in the dataset are (1) mass of land-applied biosolids calculated for NHDPlus Version 2.1 (NHDPlusV2) reach catchments in 2024 as a CSV and (2) reported amount of biosolids applied to land by county in 2024 as a CSV, reported by Virginia Department of Environmental Quality.
descript.purpose: Reported amounts of field applied biosolids were downscaled to assess the mass of land-applied biosolids within the Chesapeake Bay watershed at the NHDPlusV2 catchment and county scales Appropriate use of the data includes statistical analysis, model parameterization, and map creation or display.

procstep.procdesc: Daily Field Activity biosolids data with DEQ Control IDs were provided by the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (VA DEQ) Biosolids Program. The Daily Field Activity biosolids table included the amount of biosolids applied daily in dry tons with corresponding DEQ Control IDs. Daily amounts of biosolids at each application field were summed for the entire year of 2024. A Biosolid Areas polygon geographic layer with DEQ Control IDs was downloaded from Virginia Department of Environmental Quality.

Daily Field Activity was summed by counties. Federal Information Processing Series (FIPS) codes and sum of biosolids were exported as a CSV (“BS_mass_VA_county_2024.csv”). County data were downloaded from the U.S. Census Bureau using the “list_counties” command with the “tigris” package in RStudio.
Applied biosolids amounts were joined to the Biosolid Areas polygons layer by matching DEQ Control IDs in ArcGIS Pro.

The Biosolid Areas polygon geographic layer was imported into RStudio. Dry tons were converted to kilograms and acres were converted to square meters. A rate or density of biosolids application was calculated as a kilogram per square meter for each biosolid area. The polygon layer was converted into a 30-meter square resolution raster using this density value and the “terra ” package. The density was then multiplied by 900.

Using “exactextractr” package, the “exact_extract” function was used to summarize values from the raster created in the previous step in a table containing the sum of added biosolids within National Hydrography Dataset version 2 (NHDv2) catchments. The sum of biosolids was then converted from kilograms to pounds. The table, now containing Federal Information Processing Series (FIPS) codes and the sum of biosolids in pounds, was exported as a CSV (“BS_mass_VA_nhdv2_2024.csv”). Only catchments with an applied biosolid mass greater than zero are included in the table.
